react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the primary affected pathway. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-database, FDR = 1.27e-19, rank 1 across merged DBs) identified eight of the twelve input metabolites in this pathway: glycine (C00037), L-threonine (C00188), O-phospho-L-serine (C01005), L-cystathionine (C02291), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021), L-cysteine (C00097), guanidinoacetic acid (C00581), and adenosine 5'-monophosphate (C00020). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed the same pathway at rank 2 with p = 2.12e-08, matching six of those compounds plus a seventh overlap. Mummichog m/z-direct activity also ranked the corresponding empirical network module first (p = 0.00160), with fourteen co-varying compounds including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, guanidinoacetic acid, L-cystathionine, and L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde (C01165). A secondary but clearly distinct signal emerged for methionine metabolism / cysteine metabolism (WP:WP4292, RaMP FDR = 5.67e-13; KEGG:hsa00270, MetaboAnalystR p = 2.12e-08), driven by the S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine → L-cystathionine → L-cysteine sub-chain and supported by inorganic sulfate (C00059). Niacinamide (C00153) independently contributed to nicotinamide metabolism (mummichog p = 0.0395) and a weak NAD-biosynthesis signal, but this did not replicate across paradigms with comparable significance. The biological picture is one of coordinated disruption at the intersection of one-carbon folate-driven serine/glycine cycling and methionine/sulfur amino-acid cycling, both converging on methylation capacity (via SAH) and trans-sulfuration (via cystathionine and sulfate). Guanidinoacetic acid anchors the creatine-synthesis branch entering the glycine pool, while phosphoserine and threonine feed the serine dehydratase / glycine cleavage axis.

The MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism first (p = 0.001) and Arachidonic acid metabolism (hsa00590) second (p = 0.008). Driver-metabolite analysis identified L-Cystathionine (KEGG:C02291) and S-Adenosylhomocysteine (KEGG:C00021) as key substrates in the transsulfuration pathway connecting methionine to cysteine. react_result.final_narrative_text: The multi-paradigm pathway analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites converged on two interconnected metabolic domains: sulfur amino acid metabolism and the connected methionine cycle. The RaMP-DB enrichment (hypergeometric ORA) identified Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (hsa00260) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR 4.22e-14, followed by Cysteine and methionine metabolism (hsa00270) at rank 2 (FDR 1.38e-12). Methionine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-156581) ranked fourth with FDR 2.11e-12. The SSPa Reactome ORA confirmed strong enrichment for Sulfur amino acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1614635) at rank 3 (FDR 5.01e-12). The MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism first (p = 0.001) and Arachidonic acid metabolism (hsa00590) second (p = 0.008). The FELLA random-walk on the KEGG hierarchical graph captured indirect involvement through the connected sulfur metabolic module (hsa00920), ranking it fifth. Driver-metabolite analysis identified L-Cystathionine (KEGG:C02291) and S-Adenosylhomocysteine (KEGG:C00021) as key substrates in the transsulfuration pathway connecting methionine to cysteine. Glycine (KEGG:C00037) and L-Threonine (KEGG:C00188) contribute to the serines coupling that funnels into cysteine biosynthesis. Phosphoserine (KEGG:C01005) serves as the upstream serine precursor. These findings indicate perturbation of the methionine-cysteine transsulfuration axis with secondary effects on one-carbon folate metabolism and downstream glutathione precursor availability.

Niacinamide (C00153) independently contributed to nicotinamide metabolism (mummichog p = 0.0395) and a weak NAD-biosynthesis signal, but this did not replicate across paradigms with comparable significance. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-database, FDR = 1.27e-19, rank 1 across merged DBs) identified eight of the twelve input metabolites in this pathway: glycine (C00037), L-threonine (C00188), O-phospho-L-serine (C01005), L-cystathionine (C02291), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021), L-cysteine (C00097), guanidinoacetic acid (C00581), and adenosine 5'-monophosphate (C00020). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed the same pathway at rank 2 with p = 2.12e-08, matching six of those compounds plus a seventh overlap. Mummichog m/z-direct activity also ranked the corresponding empirical network module first (p = 0.00160), with fourteen co-varying compounds including glycine, L-threonine, phosphoserine, guanidinoacetic acid, L-cystathionine, and L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde (C01165). A secondary but clearly distinct signal emerged for methionine metabolism / cysteine metabolism (WP:WP4292, RaMP FDR = 5.67e-13; KEGG:hsa00270, MetaboAnalystR p = 2.12e-08), driven by the S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine → L-cystathionine → L-cysteine sub-chain and supported by inorganic sulfate (C00059). Niacinamide (C00153) independently contributed to nicotinamide metabolism (mummichog p = 0.0395) and a weak NAD-biosynthesis signal, but this did not replicate across paradigms with comparable significance. The biological picture is one of coordinated disruption at the intersection of one-carbon folate-driven serine/glycine cycling and methionine/sulfur amino-acid cycling, both converging on methylation capacity (via SAH) and trans-sulfuration (via cystathionine and sulfate). Guanidinoacetic acid anchors the creatine-synthesis branch entering the glycine pool, while phosphoserine and threonine feed the serine dehydratase / glycine cleavage axis.
